candidates.lead: A new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC) has taken over running of the four-day event
candidates.evidence_text: The August bank holiday weekend has been home to Manchester Pride for more than 40 years From its humble beginnings in 1985 as a fundraiser for Monsall Hospital's HIV and Aids ward, Manchester Pride grew into one of the country's biggest LGBTQ+ events When the company behind it went into voluntary liquidation last year, many were worried there would be no Pride in 2026 But Manchester City Council tried to allay fears when, in January, it announced that a new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC), Manchester Village Pride, would take over the running of the four-day event Manchester Village Pride is run by volunteer directors and is mainly made up of businesses from Manchester's Gay Village Venues in the area have loaned the new organisation £120,000 to support the planning and delivery of the event

candidates.title: Salford to extend long-term home-building plans
candidates.summary: Salford City Council sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.
candidates.practical_angle: Учитывать как новую фазу городской политики или public-affairs повестки сегодня.
candidates.lead: Salford City Council sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043
candidates.evidence_text: Salford to extend long-term home-building plans - BBC News Image caption, Mike McCusker is the council's lead member for planning By Richard Stead North West Published 1 hour ago Members of the public are being invited to have their say about plans to build nearly 35,000 new homes in Salford over the next 17 years - while also protecting the city's greenery. Extending the council's home-building plans by four years, a new document has sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043. Deputy mayor and planning boss Mike McCusker said: "We will have a brand new development plan, which will give us a good pipeline of new homes as well as protection from developers, who could successfully appeal against planning applications which the council has rejected. "At the same time its important to protect our valuable green spaces for local people." Salford Council's existing local plan, which is part of the Greater Manchester-wide Places For Everyone strategy, outlines sites to be developed until 2039. Image caption, The draft local plan outlines the ambition to build warehouses on empty land next to the Salford Community Stadium The city has been one of the fastest growing in the UK over recent years, with its population rising to 294,000 in 2024 - an increase of 34% since 2001. Most of that growth has been in the city centre - and at Salford Quays - but there have also been new homes built on former green belt land in areas like Boothstown. Councillors will vote on the draft local plan before the end of this year and it will then be submitted to the government for final approval. According to the draft plan, there will be a particular focus on development in the city centre, the Quays, Port Salford, and the site of the Salford Community Stadium. The stadium was fully acquired by the council in December 2024, when it bought Peel Land's 50% stake in the rugby ground for £7.7m. Image caption, Ivan Voronov is the leader of Reform UK on Salford Council The stadium was built in 2012 and the draft plan outlines ambitions for warehouses to be built on the empty surrounding land, supported by a possible Metrolink tram extension to Port Salford. However, Local Reform leader Ivan Voronov said: "The stadium is losing money every single year and we've been throwing good money after bad, so we should be cutting or losses on this. "Elsewhere, there's very little to support local GPs in places like Salford Quays, so how can you build another gigantic new skyscraper and not build any new medical facilities to support that?" Image caption, There are plans for 130 homes on the former St Ambrose Barlow High School site in Swinton The draft plan also includes a scheme for 130 homes on the former St Ambrose Barlow High School site in Swinton, which has been vacant since 2013. Brownfield land, which would be suitable for about 300 houses and 170 apartments, has also been identified off Orchard Street in Pendleton. There are also plans to provide an additional 35 pitches for the travelling community by extending their existing site on Duchy Road in Pendleton. The draft proposals would also give extra protection to 12 local greens, including land at Kersal Moor, Peel Park next to the University of Salford, Brickfield Wood in Boothstown and the Three Sisters nature reserve in Ellesmere Park. candidates.lead: About 8.7 million customers had their data accessed and a ransom was demanded
candidates.evidence_text: Hackers steal data from millions of UK airport customers - BBC News Image source, EPA Image caption, About 8.7 million customers across three UK airports had their data accessed By Georgie Docker and Mat Trewern , North West Published 27 August 2026 Three major UK airports have been hit by a "cyber security incident" in which criminal hackers accessed the data of almost nine million people and demanded a ransom. Manchester Airports Group (MAG), which owns Manchester, East Midlands and London Stansted airports, said customers' contact details, vehicle registrations and postcodes were obtained by hackers at the weekend. MAG told the BBC the hackers demanded a ransom fee for the return of the data, which the group said it refused to pay. The sum of the ransom fee was not disclosed. The firm said "at no point has passenger safety or aviation security been compromised" and the system hacked did not hold customers' bank or payment details. The data of about 8.7 million customers was accessed. The majority of the data accessed was restricted to customer email addresses and related to WiFi sign-ups within the airports' terminals, MAG said. MAG said in a statement: "We would like to reassure customers that Manchester Airport Group takes the security of customer information extremely seriously and we apologise for any inconvenience or concern caused." Image caption, East Midlands Airport was one of those affected, along with Manchester and London Stansted The firm said it only became aware of the hack on Tuesday and quickly prevented the hackers gaining any more access, and notified affected customers. "We immediately contained the risk and have been working with specialist advisors and taking appropriate steps to protect our customers and systems," MAG said. "We have informed and are working with the relevant authorities." Image caption, The hackers managed to steal email addresses after customers accessed WiFi in the airports The airport group said the e-mail addresses obtained by the hackers came from passengers signing up to the airports' on-site WiFi. More detailed data, including vehicle registrations, came from people booking car-park spaces, arranging access to lounges, and booking fast-track. Customers are urged to remain vigilant about suspicious emails, text messages or phone calls and avoid opening unknown attachments. 'Alarming' Michael Goddard, 71, from Cheshire, said both he and his wife, Julie, 68, had received an email earlier from MAG notifying them that their data had been breached. "I was shocked," Goddard told BBC Radio Manchester . "To find your personal info has been stolen - it is alarming. "My information has gone and I don't know what they're going to do with it. "They have my address in the form of the postcode, they've got my name, so it doesn't take too much to find out who I am. "I'm not 100% reassured by what Manchester Airports Group has said." Goddard said he received the email after travelling from East Midlands Airport earlier this year and his wife had used the online booking service for parking at Manchester Airport. "The concern is there for both of us," he said. "We want the reassurance that if anything happens, they will adequately compensate us." The identity of the hackers was known, MAG said, and the relevant authorities had been informed. The Information Commissioner's Office said it was assessing the incident. "We can confirm we have received a breach report from Manchester Airports Group, and we are assessing the information provided," a spokesperson said. The organisation said anyone concerned by the breach was able to access support on the ICO website , external . candidates.lead: Work will begin on replacing the M6 Thelwall Viaduct's joints on 1 September
candidates.evidence_text: Speed limits and lane closures for M6 viaduct upgrade works - BBC News Image source, Anthony O'Neill/Geograph Image caption, The viaduct's joints have "reached the end of their operational lifespan", National Highways says By Georgie Docker North West Published 27 August 2026 Speed limits and lane closures are being imposed on a motorway viaduct as work is carried out to replace its bridge joints. The £27m "essential" upgrade will begin on the Thelwall Viaduct on the M6 in Lymm, Warrington, on 1 September. A full time contraflow system will be introduced from 12 October, as well as a temporary 40 mph (64 kmh) speed limit and narrow lanes. National Highways said the viaduct, which crosses the Manchester Ship Canal and the River Mersey, was "built several decades ago" and the work was needed for safety reasons. Work will be done on one carriage way at a time. Image source, Peter McDermott/Geograph Image caption, Work will be carried out overnight All lanes - northbound and southbound - will stay open during the day, with one lane open overnight on the carriageway being worked on. "Our road network is ageing, and many key structures, including Thelwall Viaduct, were built several decades ago," Chris Court from National Highways said. "The viaduct's joints have now reached the end of their operational lifespan, making replacement essential to maintain safety and reliability for road users." The project is due to be completed by the beginning of 2028. candidates.evidence_text: Swinton Park Golf Club: 700 homes proposed for former course - BBC News Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, The former Swinton Park Golf Club site has been closed since September 2020 By Charlotte Hall , Local Democracy Reporting Service and Haider Saleem , Reporting from North West Published 27 August 2026 Proposals for about 700 homes on a former golf course have raised residents‘ concerns about traffic and pressure on local services. Wain Estates is consulting on the future of the 100-acre former Swinton Park Golf Club site in Swinton, Greater Manchester, which closed in September 2020. The developer said more than half the site could become public open space, with affordable homes, sports facilities and housing for older people also proposed. But Mike Hartney, 65, who has lived in the area for 34 years, said traffic was already "awful" and local services were oversubscribed. "Everywhere is oversubscribed already," he said. "It'll only get worse." Wain Estates said it intended to seek outline planning permission later in 2026 and the number of homes could change following technical work, public feedback and discussions with council planners. Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, Mike Hartney said traffic and local services were already under pressure Dave Marsh, who was a member of the golf club for more than 30 years, said the course should be restored. Mr Marsh, who campaigns with Save Swinton Park Golf Club, said the grounds had remained closed throughout the coronavirus pandemic, despite appeals from the community. "It never should have closed as a golf club," he said. "We will fight it until our last breath to stop them." However, not all residents opposed developing the land. Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, Sam Hope said new homes could benefit families, but raised concerns about congestion Sam Hope, 41, said new homes could help first-time buyers and families unable to afford some existing properties in Swinton and nearby Monton. "If they do what they've done here in terms of green space, make a bigger park, maybe even add a coffee shop, then we could use it," she said. But she added that another 700 homes could worsen congestion and said the area did not have the "right infrastructure". The proposals include a main entrance from the East Lancashire Road through a traffic-controlled junction and an emergency access route from Cliftonville Drive. Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, Developer Wain Estates said it intended to seek outline planning permission later in 2026 Wain Estates acquired the company which owned the golf club in April 2021. The site is privately owned, has no public rights of way and has remained unused since the club closed. Neil Lewis, the company's planning director, said the firm wanted to hear residents' views. "Our proposals look to bring historically private land back into use, creating a new place with a range of benefits for the wider community," he said. "This would include new sports facilities, walking and cycling routes, alongside a range of new homes of different sizes and tenures." He said the company envisaged a "green and welcoming development", with more than half the site remaining as publicly accessible open space. An outline application would seek permission for the principle of developing the land, rather than approval of the detailed design of individual homes. The consultation is due to close on 20 September. candidates.evidence_text: The August bank holiday weekend has been home to Manchester Pride for more than 40 years From its humble beginnings in 1985 as a fundraiser for Monsall Hospital's HIV and Aids ward, Manchester Pride grew into one of the country's biggest LGBTQ+ events When the company behind it went into voluntary liquidation last year, many were worried there would be no Pride in 2026 But Manchester City Council tried to allay fears when, in January, it announced that a new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC), Manchester Village Pride, would take over the running of the four-day event Manchester Village Pride is run by volunteer directors and is mainly made up of businesses from Manchester's Gay Village Venues in the area have loaned the new organisation £120,000 to support the planning and delivery of the event

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Changes to former Bolton NatWest bank ordered to be torn down after being built without permission Planning enforcement has been instigated at a former NatWest building which dates back to Victorian times Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy Metal shutters and an extension built without planning permission at a former bank have been ordered to be ripped down In the past few months three metal lean-to shutters have been installed along the side of the former NatWest building on the corner of Church Street, Farnworth, along with an extension. Bolton council has said no planning permission was previously applied for or approved for the The enforcement notice, published by the council, states that subject to any appeal being lodged, the unauthorised extension must be demolished and the roller shutter doors must be removed within two months of notice taking effect on September 30 A third condition of the enforcement notice states: “Restore the south principal elevation of the building to its condition immediately before the unauthorised development took place “This includes but is not limited to, the repair of the original elevation removed or damaged during the construction works using materials to match the original building in appearance, colour, texture and finish.”

candidates.evidence_text: Health 'Deeply concerning' data reveals sexual misconduct allegations in doctor tribunals "These figures paint a deeply concerning picture for those working in healthcare" News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer and Ella Pickover 15:40, 27 More than a third of sexual misconduct allegation types heard by medical tribunals in the past year involved healthcare colleagues, new figures show A leading judge has called the figures "deeply concerning," warning that health workers should be "free to do their jobs without fear of becoming a target of sexual misconduct" after data showed the proportion of doctor tribunals involving sexual misconduct against a colleague The Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service (MPTS) recorded 270 allegation types across 160 tribunal hearings in 2025, with 48 relating to sexual misconduct. Of those sexual misconduct allegations, 18 involved colleagues and 17 involved patients A further 11 involved other people, including online offences, while two involved a relative or someone known to the doctor. The figures have prompted the MPTS to call for the data to be used as part of a wider conversation about how sexual misconduct can be prevented and address MPTS chairwoman Judge Fiona Monk said: “These figures paint a deeply concerning picture for those working in healthcare

Hackers accessed data relating to car park, lounge and fast track bookings and in-airport WIFI s The data included people's email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registrations and postcodes. The group said 'at no point has passenger safety or aviation security been compromised' during the incident and neither MAG nor the system hacked held customers’ bank or payment detail Today people affected are receiving emails about the hack. The email says: "We're contacting you about a recent cyber security incident involving customer data "Our investigation has identified that some of your personal information relating to airport car parking, lounge, Fast Track bookings and on-airport WIFI sign-ups has been accessed by an unauthorised third party."

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Changes to former Bolton NatWest bank ordered to be torn down after being built without permission Planning enforcement has been instigated at a former NatWest building which dates back to Victorian times Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy Metal shutters and an extension built without planning permission at a former bank have been ordered to be ripped down In the past few months three metal lean-to shutters have been installed along the side of the former NatWest building on the corner of Church Street, Farnworth, along with an extension. Bolton council has said no planning permission was previously applied for or approved for the The enforcement notice, published by the council, states that subject to any appeal being lodged, the unauthorised extension must be demolished and the roller shutter doors must be removed within two months of notice taking effect on September 30 A third condition of the enforcement notice states: “Restore the south principal elevation of the building to its condition immediately before the unauthorised development took place “This includes but is not limited to, the repair of the original elevation removed or damaged during the construction works using materials to match the original building in appearance, colour, texture and finish.”

candidates.evidence_text: Blackley Manchester's new 'mega church' that could see up to 1,100 turning up to services It was approved by councillors Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 06:10, 28 Aug 2026 View 2 Images A new 'mega' church will be built in Blackley A ‘mega church’ will be built in Blackley despite fears about a massive influx of traffic. The 5,000 sqm building will be built on Chain Road after the demolition of former convent buildings on the land, and could have 1,100 people turning up for services at one time on its busie World Mission Agency, which is currently based on Broughton Lane in Salford , is behind the plans for the new church to meet demand for its ‘growing congregation’ It was originally supposed to have a maximum of 1,500 people attending its special services at any one time, but the numbers were scaled back after ‘concerns’ about how it could pile pressure on the roads The plans have caused controversy in Blackley , leading to 25 objections from neighbours, who said the area ‘cannot support such a large flow of more traffic’ Despite the fears, the plans were approved unanimously by Manchester council's planning committee on Thursday

candidates.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Andy Burnham sparks political row as he says Irish unity poll ‘off the table’ The Prime Minister was making his first visit to Northern Ireland since taking office Comments News Jonathan McCambridge , Claudia Savage , Rebecca Black and Am Andy Burnham has sparked a political row during his first visit to Northern Ireland as Prime Minister after he stated that an Irish border poll is “off the table” Sinn Féin leader Mary Lou McDonald reacted strongly to the remarks, stating that no prime minister has the right to “high-handedly” remove the provision for a unity referendum from the Good Friday Agreement However, DUP leader Gavin Robinson welcomed the comments, stating the Prime Minister had “put to bed the nonsense” speculation over a unity poll, the Press Association reports During his visit to Belfast Mr Burnham said he is “here to listen” but added that the “rifts” arising from referendums “take a long time to heal”, referring to Brexit and the Scottish independence referendum Under the terms of the 1998 Belfast/Good Friday Agreement, the Secretary of State can decide to hold a border poll, and it also places a duty on the office holder to call one if it appears likely a majority would vote for Irish unification

candidates.evidence_text: Solar Eclipse Will you have clear skies for the lunar eclipse? Check your postcode Stargazers across the country could catch a glimpse of the celestial event as the Sun, Earth and Moon align, causing the Earth to cast its shadow across the lunar surfa People in Manchester will have the chance to see the Moon turn an eerie shade of red in the early hours of Friday as a spectacular lunar eclipse takes place over the UK Stargazers across the country could catch a glimpse of the celestial event as the Sun, Earth and Moon align, causing the Earth to cast its shadow across the lunar surface The deep partial lunar eclipse will take place in the early hours of August 28, when around 93% of the Moon is expected to be covered by the darkest part of Earth's shadow at the peak of the event But whether people will actually be able to see the eclipse will depend heavily on the weather , with cloud cover expected to threaten views in several parts of the UK The Met Office has warned that "conditions are expected to be challenging for many hoping to see the eclipse", although southern and eastern England are expected to have the best chance of catching at least part of the spectacle

candidates.evidence_text: Trafford Trafford council could lose control of children's services after seven years of 'failure' 'They do not get their childhood back while we improve the process' Comments News Hannah Richardson 17:14, 27 Aug 2026 View 3 Images An emergency counci Trafford council could lose control of children’s services as the government steps in to deal with the crisis-hit department A recent Ofsted inspection saw the service rated ‘inadequate’ by the education watchdog , the lowest possible rating. Inspectors found children were being left in ‘potentially unsafe situations for too long’ because of delays in initial responses Some of the problems identified by inspectors were branded ‘serious and significant’, and in some cases ‘unrealistic expectations’ were being placed on children ‘to keep themselves safe’. Town hall bosses did not ‘fully’ grasp the extent of the issues until they were pointed out Council leadership apologised for the failings found in the service, saying work to improve the services is under way and thanking staff for their professionalism and commitment Just a week later, the council received a second critical report, this time into its Adult Social Care department . Healthcare inspectors from the Care Quality Commission found long waits; low satisfaction; and ‘ineffective’ sharing of safeguarding lessons but noted improvements

candidates.lead: Manchester Airport Why millions of people are getting emails from Manchester Airport today Around 8.7 million people's data has been accessed in a hack at the Manchester Airports Group (MAG) Comments News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter Millions of people have recei
candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Why millions of people are getting emails from Manchester Airport today Around 8.7 million people's data has been accessed in a hack at the Manchester Airports Group (MAG) Comments News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter Millions of people have received emails from the Manchester Airports Group (MAG) following a major cyber hack The company, which operates Manchester Airport , London Stansted and East Midlands Airport, has sent emails to the 8.7 million customers affected by the data breach earlier this week. Hackers accessed data relating to car park, lounge and fast track bookings and in-airport WIFI s The data included people's email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registrations and postcodes. The group said 'at no point has passenger safety or aviation security been compromised' during the incident and neither MAG nor the system hacked held customers’ bank or payment detail Today people affected are receiving emails about the hack. The email says: "We're contacting you about a recent cyber security incident involving customer data "Our investigation has identified that some of your personal information relating to airport car parking, lounge, Fast Track bookings and on-airport WIFI sign-ups has been accessed by an unauthorised third party."

As the man fell to the ground, the group launched a violent attack, during which he was repeatedly hit a machete Despite attempting to hold on, the group stole his electric bike and fled. He was left with a number of serious injuries including a severe laceration to his thumb, and cuts to his face Cox, of Salford , was jailed for 10 years earlier this week after previously pleading guilty to robbery, burglary with intent to steal and a further two counts of burglary where bikes were stolen during both incidents. He must serve at least seven-and-a-half years before he will View 4 Images Kade Cox and two other masked individuals riding on the pavement (Image: Greater Manchester Police) In footage shared by Greater Manchester Police , the group can be seen riding on motorbikes around the Sale area. candidates.evidence_text: Trafford Trafford council could lose control of children's services after seven years of 'failure' 'They do not get their childhood back while we improve the process' Comments News Hannah Richardson 17:14, 27 Aug 2026 View 3 Images An emergency counci Trafford council could lose control of children’s services as the government steps in to deal with the crisis-hit department A recent Ofsted inspection saw the service rated ‘inadequate’ by the education watchdog , the lowest possible rating. Inspectors found children were being left in ‘potentially unsafe situations for too long’ because of delays in initial responses Some of the problems identified by inspectors were branded ‘serious and significant’, and in some cases ‘unrealistic expectations’ were being placed on children ‘to keep themselves safe’. Town hall bosses did not ‘fully’ grasp the extent of the issues until they were pointed out Council leadership apologised for the failings found in the service, saying work to improve the services is under way and thanking staff for their professionalism and commitment Just a week later, the council received a second critical report, this time into its Adult Social Care department . Healthcare inspectors from the Care Quality Commission found long waits; low satisfaction; and ‘ineffective’ sharing of safeguarding lessons but noted improvements

Tahir Rashid, 55; Mohammed Saleem, 47; Sucklane Shah, 47; Amjad Mahmood, 54; Iftaq Hussain, 46; and Arshad Mohammed, 56, deny all the charges they fac View 2 Images The trial is being heard at Minshull Street Crown Court (Image: MEN Media) Mr Mahmood is not present in the dock at Minshull Street Crown Court. The court has been told he is receiving treatment in a foreign hospital for a 'complex psychiatric illness' and 'through no fault of his own is unfit to stand trial.'

candidates.evidence_text: Health 'Deeply concerning' data reveals sexual misconduct allegations in doctor tribunals "These figures paint a deeply concerning picture for those working in healthcare" News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer and Ella Pickover 15:40, 27 More than a third of sexual misconduct allegation types heard by medical tribunals in the past year involved healthcare colleagues, new figures show A leading judge has called the figures "deeply concerning," warning that health workers should be "free to do their jobs without fear of becoming a target of sexual misconduct" after data showed the proportion of doctor tribunals involving sexual misconduct against a colleague The Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service (MPTS) recorded 270 allegation types across 160 tribunal hearings in 2025, with 48 relating to sexual misconduct. Of those sexual misconduct allegations, 18 involved colleagues and 17 involved patients A further 11 involved other people, including online offences, while two involved a relative or someone known to the doctor. The figures have prompted the MPTS to call for the data to be used as part of a wider conversation about how sexual misconduct can be prevented and address MPTS chairwoman Judge Fiona Monk said: “These figures paint a deeply concerning picture for those working in healthcare

candidates.lead: Manchester Airport Why millions of people are getting emails from Manchester Airport today Around 8.7 million people's data has been accessed in a hack at the Manchester Airports Group (MAG) Comments News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter Millions of people have recei
candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Why millions of people are getting emails from Manchester Airport today Around 8.7 million people's data has been accessed in a hack at the Manchester Airports Group (MAG) Comments News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter Millions of people have received emails from the Manchester Airports Group (MAG) following a major cyber hack The company, which operates Manchester Airport , London Stansted and East Midlands Airport, has sent emails to the 8.7 million customers affected by the data breach earlier this week. Hackers accessed data relating to car park, lounge and fast track bookings and in-airport WIFI s The data included people's email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registrations and postcodes. The group said 'at no point has passenger safety or aviation security been compromised' during the incident and neither MAG nor the system hacked held customers’ bank or payment detail Today people affected are receiving emails about the hack. The email says: "We're contacting you about a recent cyber security incident involving customer data "Our investigation has identified that some of your personal information relating to airport car parking, lounge, Fast Track bookings and on-airport WIFI sign-ups has been accessed by an unauthorised third party."

We the people of Manchester ask Manchester City Council to protect and support Market Street stalls."

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Monday 27 July 2026 at 4:49pm Play Brightcove video ITV Granada Reports' political correspondent Lise McNally explains the Supplementary Vote (SV) system More than 2 million voters are gearing up for one of the biggest by-elections in political history On Thursday 30th July, polls will open across all ten Greater Manchester boroughs, so people can choose who should replace Andy Burnham as the region's new Metro Mayor It's a role with considerable devolved powers - the Mayor represents the region nationally and internationally, and is tasked with improving the everyday lives of people across Bolton, Bury, Manchester, Oldham, Rochdale, Salford, Stockport, Tameside, Trafford and Wigan The policy areas they are in charge of include transport, planning, the police, and driving economic growth A voting system called the Supplementary Vote (SV) will be in place for the Greater Manchester mayoral election, as opposed to first past the post, the system used for a general election

Credit: Greater Manchester Police A man who killed a teenage boy on an e-bike after ramming him with his car has been jailed for 17 years Terrence King, 60, was found guilty of killing Devon Simmonds-Caines after deliberately driving his car into him on Rowrah Crescent in Middleton , Manchester King had been chasing the e-bike, which had been reportedly stolen, steering his vehicle directly at the teenager at speed without braking, on 22 July 2025 Emergency services immediately attended but despite their best efforts, Devon, aged 15, was died at the scene King was found guilty of murder at Manchester Crown Court on 17 July Following his death, Devon's family released a tribute , calling him a "bubbly person" who "only wanted the best for everyone around him"

Credit: PNW Vote before the end of 26 August to have your say on the building that has had the greatest impact on the city Place North West went to our readers with a question earlier this month: What is Manchester’s most important building? We kept the question purposefully vague – did importance mean visual impact? Economic or cultural benefits? A project that inspires others and over time brings a We did provide some criteria though: the building had to be completed within the past 100 years and it must be in Manchester proper Pulling from those responses we crafted a shortlist. Now the time has come to determine a winner. The poll opened on 12 August and closes at the end of the day on 26 August. candidates.evidence_text: One of Manchester’s best-known hospitality operators has taken on a children’s nursery in New Moston Ross Mackenzie, who founded the Liars Club Group/ Crazy Pedro’s and built and sold the Black Dog Ballroom bars, has taken ownership of Nuthurst Day Care on Nuthurst Road. The nursery opens in September for children aged six months to five years It is an unlikely move for a man who has spent three decades in licensed retail, and Mackenzie is the first to say so On this new move, he commented; “Hospitality and childcare have more in common than people assume. Both come down to people walking through your door and trusting you with a few hours of their day. The stakes are just very different, and I don’t take that lightly “I’ve spent thirty years building places people actually want to be in. I want Nuthurst to be that for the families of New Moston.” The nursery, at 204 Nuthurst Road, has been fully refurbished up over the summer ahead of the September opening. It has three rooms, named Hedgehogs, Squirrels and Owls, and a large garden overlooking Nuthurst Park

candidates.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email A blue plaque has been unveiled at a Bowdon house to mark the life of William Wood, the social reformer known as “The Climbing Boys’ Friend” The plaque is at Willow Cottage, 28 Stamford Road, where Wood lived after retiring there in 1847. It was unveiled last week at a ceremony organised by Trafford Council’s Local Studies team, attended by residents, historians, council members, Connor Rand MP and the Friends of Bowd Wood, born in 1782, was a wool merchant who began campaigning in 1826 after seeing a young boy fall to his death inside a chimney onto a live fire. “Climbing boys” were children sent up chimneys to sweep them, often suffering burns, respiratory illness, deformity and suffocation From Bowdon he funded prosecutions against master sweeps who broke child labour laws, put up placards at railway stations and wrote to newspapers He also challenged magistrates and even Queen Victoria over the use of a child sweep at Windsor Castle His work with Lord Shaftesbury included testimony to the House of Lords in 1853, which helped lead to the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875. Wood died in 1868, aged 85, seven years before the practice was banned. Six chimney sweeps from five towns carried his coffin to St Mary’s Churc

It was unveiled last week at a ceremony organised by Trafford Council’s Local Studies team, attended by residents, historians, council members, Connor Rand MP and the Friends of Bowd Wood, born in 1782, was a wool merchant who began campaigning in 1826 after seeing a young boy fall to his death inside a chimney onto a live fire. “Climbing boys” were children sent up chimneys to sweep them, often suffering burns, respiratory illness, deformity and suffocation From Bowdon he funded prosecutions against master sweeps who broke child labour laws, put up placards at railway stations and wrote to newspapers He also challenged magistrates and even Queen Victoria over the use of a child sweep at Windsor Castle His work with Lord Shaftesbury included testimony to the House of Lords in 1853, which helped lead to the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875. Wood died in 1868, aged 85, seven years before the practice was banned. Six chimney sweeps from five towns carried his coffin to St Mary’s Churc

A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment The site was vacated later that day. candidates.lead: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture
candidates.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture From theatre, film and music to a new mural and giant fuzzy felt artwork, the projects cover a wide range of art forms and celebrate Oldham’s people, places and stories Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up . Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. Isobel and Fay will reimagine it for today using patchwork and running-stitch embroidery Local people will be invited to add buildings and places that are important to them, using old clothes and fabric from home

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Council's Community Safety Service received a Closure Order for a house following reports of persistent anti-social behaviour and criminal activity The order, which is in place for three months, was granted by magistrates under the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014. The order makes it an offence for anyone, including the occupants, from entering the property while it is in force and restricts access only to Reports linked to the address included disorderly and intimidating behaviour, suspected drug-related activity and the order aims to provide respite to residents and protect them from disruption Closure Orders can be obtained by councils and police where a property is linked to serious nuisance, disorder or criminal activity The order will remain in place for three months initially. The court can extend it for a further three months if necessary, and longer-term measures may also be considered to prevent future problems and protect the local community Residents played a vital role in securing the order by providing information and evidence about the issues affecting the area

candidates.evidence_text: A new strategy aims to help everyone in Bolton live a healthy, connected and fulfilling life, supported by strong communities, active environments and quality homes The Joint Local Health and Wellbeing (JHWS) Strategy 2026–2029 sets out how organisations across the borough will work together to improve health and wellbeing and reduce health inequalities The strategy has been approved by Bolton's Health and Wellbeing Board, which brings together leaders from local government, public health, social care, the NHS, housing, the voluntary and community sector, and other key partners The strategy places a strong emphasis on prevention, recognising that helping people stay healthy is just as important as treating illness when it occurs It provides a shared framework for partners to take collective action on the factors that have the biggest impact on people's health and wellbeing The Health and Wellbeing Board has identified three priorities where its collective leadership can add the greatest value

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. candidates.evidence_text: Grub on the Docks - Media City UK Street Food Line-Up: Featuring Sizzling Seoul, Dukes Po Boys, and more Grub on the Docks Venue Gardens Dates 28 th May - 20 th Sep '26 Open Tuesday to Sunday weekly, 12 noon – 10pm GRUB on the Docks is bringing the flavour this summer – think unreal street food, ice-cold drinks and non-stop vibes right in the MediaCity gardens, on the waterfront. We’re talking a stacked rotation of indie food like Sizzling Seoul, Umami Cartel, Oppa Korean Dogs and more, switching it up every week so there’s always something new to try. NEW challenge, take on the BELLY BUSTER CHALLENGE from CAFF – sausage. bacon. egg. black pudding. hash brown. All packed into one proper Belly Buster bap for £7.50. Time to beat is 5 minutes set the fastest finishing time and your next Belly Buster is FREE . EVENTS Wine on the Docks Every Wednesday | All day, venue hours Midweek just got better. Every Wednesday, buy two glasses of the same wine and we’ll top up the rest of the bottle on us. No catch, no fuss just a proper reason to make Wednesday your new favourite day. Sunset Sessions Every Friday | 5–8pm Clock off and head straight to the water’s edge. A rotating line-up of DJs kicks off the weekend early, with a trader special and a featured drinks offer to match. Same time, same spot, every Friday, your after-work wind-down sorted. Paws on the Docks 8 AUGUST | 22 AUGUST | 5 SEPTEMBER | 19 SEPTEMBER | Mornings Bring the dog, grab a coffee, make a morning of it. Paws on the Docks is our relaxed dog-friendly social – think breakfast specials, water bowls, complimentary pup cups and market stalls that welcome four-legged visitors as warmly as the two-legged ones. Residents social Thursday 20th August – 5pm to 7pm An evening for all MediaCity residents, with a DJ playing live on the docks. A nice informal social, come down, grab a drink and meet other residents at our waterfront setting. Media Makers Mixer Thursday 27th August – 5pm to 7pm A regular hosted networking event for MediaCity’s creative and production community, designed to bring people together and encourage connections across the area. Be the first in the know Sign up to receive email updates on the latest events, news and offers at MediaCity Visit our privacy policy here. candidates.evidence_text: Dame Meera Syal joins us to share the hilarious and heartwarming true stories that have shaped her life and work as one of Britain’s most beloved comedy legends Growing up in the only Asian family in a West Midlands mining village, Meera Syal wanted to take the stage long before anyone was ready to listen As one of the creators of Goodness Gracious Me, she changed British comedy forever. As the indomitable Granny Ummi, she terrified the guests visiting The Kumars at Number 42. She’s topped the pop charts, been a Professor at Oxford, and written a musical with Andrew Lloyd Webber. From the wisdom her mother and aunties dispensed, her grandfather’s attempts to arrange her marriage, her working life as an actress and writer, her journey to motherhood, and the changing attitudes towards women she has experienced over her career, Meera will share all. One of the largest Victorian walled gardens in the UK, it showcases a range of growing techniques and edible plants There’s also the spectacular Paradise Garden showcasing exotic planting inspired by Asiatic and Mediterranean gardens. The orchard and nearby bee and butterfly garden, have been designed to attract wildlife The Peel Learning Garden, supported by The Peel Group, will help schoolchildren learn how plants affect our lives and the planet, whilst the Community Wellbeing Garden provides a space for people to garden, socialise and relax

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

The evening kicks off early downstairs at 7pm with a laid-back, candlelit soundtrack of live soul and neo-soul. Manchester's Springtime Feast is returning to Wythenshawe Park & Gardens for its BIGGEST celebration to date! After an incredible 2025 event, we’re heading to the back to the stunning fields of Wythenshawe Park & Gardens for a weekend jam-packed with brand-new production, eccentric live entertainment, and an abundance of culinary delights 🌳 Alongside the cornerstone classics, you can expect Mark the date, grab your family and friends, and lock yourselves in for Manchester's ultimate foodie celebration this Spring. Last year tickets were snapped up faster than Yorkshire puds at a Sunday Roast... don't hang about - get yours before they're all gone! Join thousands of Stroll through the peaceful green fields of Wythenshawe Park and follow the tempting scents of world flavours as they lead you on a global adventure courtesy of some of the UK’s best street food traders. Именно здесь украинское хип-хоп трио KAVABANGA DEPO KOLIBRI снова выйдет на сцену, чтобы презентовать свою новую музыку.
